destinations.title: Swat
destinations.description: The lush green and historic Swat Valley, in the Malakand Division lies between 34o - 40' to 35o N latitude and 72' to 74o - 6’ E longitude and is part of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. The valley is an integral part of the strategic and significant region where three parts of the Asian Continent—South Asia, Central Asia and China meet. The names found in ancient sources for Swat are Udyana and Suvastu because of the scenic beauty of the valley and the name of the river, respectively. The historical and cultural remains of the area provide evidence about human activities covering a large span of time. Alexander the Great came here in 327 BC en route India. In ancient times it remained center of Buddhism, still having its marks found from river bed to the tops of the mountains. During Abdul Wadud (1917- 1949) and Jahan Zeb's (1949-1969) peaceful region, Swati territories forming part of Swat State witnessed unprecedented development in the fields of education, health and communication. The magnificent Swat Valley popularly known as the Switzerland of the East, is situated north of Peshawar. In ancient times, it remained center of the then flourishing Buddhist civilization, still having its remnants found at various places. Its old name was Udyana (Land of Gardens). The archeological sites and monasteries dating back to Buddhist era add to its historical charm. Surrounded by majestic mountains, Swat Valley is full of roaring rivers, lush green forests and snow-covered peaks adding to its natural attraction. "Upper” and " Lower " Swat are terms in vogue based on the arbitrary demarcation of higher and lower regions In the valley by Swat River. Green fruit orchards, beautiful lakes, gushing streams and a fascinating landscape make it a place worth seeing.

destinations.title: Abbottabad
destinations.description:
It is charming spread out over several low, refreshingly
cool, and green hills. Abbottabad is 116 km (2 hours) from Rawalpindi and 208 km
(3 hours) from Peshawar. Abbottabad, which is 1,250 m approximately above sea level,
is a neat and clean town in a spacious valley surrounded by green hills. It is
a popular summer resort. It serves as a base for trips to Kaghan Valley and the
Gallies. KP-CTA maintains a Tourist Information Centre here to facilitate

with a water spring, and the Shimla Hill viewpoint. Thandiani is another attractive
hill resort 30 km east of Abbottabad at an altitude of 2,800 meters above sea
level.

destinations.title: Swabi
destinations.description:
Swabi District Lies Between The Indus Rivers And Kabul Rivers. Swabi District Is Now Home To Many Excellent Educational Institutes But There Was No Public Sector University Till 2012. The Only Degree Awarding Institution Then Was Private Sector Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute Of Engineering Sciences And Technology, Which Was Inaugurated In 1993. In 2012, Government Of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Established First Public Sector University In Swabi, When It Upgraded Abdul Wali Khan University Mardan-Swabi Campus Into Full-Fledged University Of Swabi. While Women University Swabi Was Established In 2016, Swabi District Also Has A Public Sector Medical College Gajju Khan Medical College Swabi Which Was Established In 2014. Swabi District Is Currently Subdivided Into 4 Tehsils; Swabi Tehsil, Topi Tehsil, Lahor Tehsil And Razzar Tehsil.
 Swabi's historical significance is interwoven with its cultural fabric, evident in its archaeological sites like the ancient city of Raja Mehmoodabad. The district's strong Pashtun traditions infuse warmth, hospitality, and a sense of community. As a region advancing toward progress, Swabi has become an economic center driven by agriculture, commerce, and emerging industries. Its educational institutions contribute to intellectual growth, symbolizing the district's commitment to modernization.

destinations.title: Mardan
destinations.description: Mardan, District headquarter, the biggest town of Yousafzais and once the centre of Gandhara Civilisation, includes Takht-iBhai, Sahri Bahlol, Jamal Garhi, Shahbaz Garhi, Sikri, Chanaka Dheri and Palo Dheri as major Buddhist sites of Gandhara. A museum in Mardan has been recently opened. From Mardan, one can go to Shahbaz Garhi on Swabi road, where the Ashoka Rock Edicts are located. Many Buddhist legends are associated with this place, which is located at a distance of 15 km from Mardan. From here, the road goes further up to Asota Megaliths (’Stonehenge of Pakistan’) nearShiwa Adda on the Swabi Mardan road, and then to Swabi. At Swabi, the road bifurcates, one leading to Hund, the last capital of Gandhara under the Shahi rulers from the 7th-10th century AD. Mardan's historical significance is deeply ingrained, with ancient sites like the Takht-i-Bahi Buddhist monastery standing as testaments to its past. As the epicenter of Gandhara civilization, the district resonates with echoes of a rich history, while its Pashtun culture infuses warmth, hospitality, and a strong sense of community. Amidst this cultural legacy, Mardan has embraced progress, emerging as an economic hub driven by agriculture, commerce, and industries. The district's educational institutions contribute to intellectual growth, empowering future generations and paving the way for innovation and modernization.

destinations.title: Haripur
destinations.description:
Haripur District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, presents an intriguing blend of tradition and modernity. This district, characterized by its diverse population and cultural heritage, offers a captivating glimpse into the fusion of past and present. Festivals, crafts, and cuisine celebrate the vibrant cultural expressions that thrive amidst the backdrop of scenic landscapes, where rolling hills and fertile valleys create a serene ambiance.
 Economically vibrant, Haripur stands as a pivotal center of commerce, boasting a thriving industrial sector alongside its agrarian roots. Its educational landscape is equally impressive, with notable institutions nurturing intellectual growth and paving the way for progress. As the district strides forward, its commitment to sustainable development and enhanced social services positions Haripur as a promising destination for both cultural exploration and modern pursuits.

destinations.title: Mansehra
destinations.description: Mansehra District Is In The Hazara Division Of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province Of Pakistan. Mansehra District And Town Are Named After Man Singh, A Leading General Of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Mansehra Makes Its Boundary On The North To Kohistan And Battagram Districts, On The East To Muzaffarabad District Of Azad Jammu & Kashmir, On The South To Abbottabad And Haripur Districts And On The West To Shangla And Buner Districts. Mansehra District Is Dominated By High Mountains, The Famous Babusar Pass Is Situated On The North-Eastern Boundary Of The District. The Climate Is Cold In Much Winter And Pleasantly Warm In Summer. The Northern Part Like Kaghan Valley Is Cold In Summer And Extremely Cold In Winter And It Receives Heavy Snow Fall. The District Is Very Famous From The Tourism Point Of View And Has Been Blessed With Wonderful Scenery. Some Of Mansehra's Main Features Are Mountain Ranges, Plains, Valleys, And Numerous Lakes And Rivers. The Main Tourist Sites In The District Include Baffa, Dadar, Balakot, Kaghan Valley, Oghi, Shogran, Naran And The Famous Shrines Of Shah Ahmad Shaheed And Shah Ismail Shaheed, Who Fought The Battle With Sikhs In 19th Century, Are Also Historic Places To Visit. There Are Three Famous Lakes In The District: Lulusar Lake, Dudipatsar Lake And Saiful Muluk Lake.

destinations.title: Peshawar
destinations.description:
The Po-Lu-Shah of the Chinese, Pushapura of Persians and
Peshawar of the Mughal rulers the present capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
province of Pakistan was the second Capital of Gandhara under the Kushanas from
1-5th century AD it is the oldest surviving city in this part of Asia. Here,
once stood Asia’s biggest and most famous Stupa of Kanishka at Shahji ki Dheri,
outside the walled city’s Gunj Gate. The site was excavated in 1906-7 by D.B.
Spooner, the then curator of Peshawar Museum. The bronze relic casket
containing a crystal reliquary of Kanishka’s time was recovered from here. It
is now on display in the Peshawar Museum. The relics consisting of bones of
Buddha were gifted by the British rulers to the Buddhist Association of Burma
in 1910 and are now housed in the main pagoda in Mandalay. The Chinese
pilgrims, who visited Gandhara during 5th century AD, spoke of the glory and
richness of the Buddhist stupas and monasteries, especially the Kanishka stupa
and the famous Alms Bowl of Buddha displayed at one time in Peshawar. Gor
Khatri, Mahabbat Khan Mosque, Balahisar, Qissa Khawni Bazar, Mohallah Sethian,
Islamia College, Edwardes College, All Saints’ Church and St Jhon’s Cathedral,
Tomb of Nawab Syed Khan inside Mission Hospital, Durrani Graveyard, Governor’s
House and Peshawar Museum are some important features of Peshawar that merit a
visit.

destinations.title: Lower Dir
destinations.description:
Lower Dir District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, presents a captivating blend of natural beauty and historical significance. Its landscapes, adorned with rolling hills, fertile valleys, and meandering rivers, reflect nature's artistry, drawing nature enthusiasts to explore its scenic trails and discover the allure of the Hindu Kush mountains in the backdrop.
 Lower Dir's cultural heritage is deeply rooted in its rich history, with remnants of past civilizations interwoven into its tapestry. The district has witnessed the ebb and flow of various empires, from ancient times to more recent eras. As a historic crossroads, it has been influenced by the diverse cultures that traversed its lands along the ancient Silk Road. The legacy of these interactions can still be felt in the traditional practices, indigenous craftsmanship, and warm hospitality of its communities, offering visitors a genuine glimpse into its past.

destinations.title: Upper Dir
destinations.description:
Upper Dir is a picturesque district located in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. It is renowned for its stunning natural beauty, diverse landscapes, and rich cultural heritage. Situated in the northern part of the province, Upper Dir shares borders with Afghanistan to the west, the district of Lower Dir to the south, Swat district to the east, and Chitral district to the north.
 The district's landscape is characterized by lush green valleys, rolling hills, snow-capped mountains, and glistening rivers. It is a part of the larger Malakand Division and is known for its temperate climate, making it an attractive destination for both domestic and international tourists.
 Upper Dir is primarily inhabited by ethnic Pashtuns, and the Pashto language is widely spoken. The local culture is deeply rooted in Pashtun traditions, with traditional music, dances, and hospitality being integral parts of daily life.

destinations.title: Chitral Upper
destinations.description:
Under the shadows of Tirichmir in the Hindukush mountain
range, the valley of Chitral in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan is a
fascinating combination of scenic beauty and cultural diversity. The land of
majestic mountains, lakes, glaciers, and snow-covered peaks. Chitral stretches
from 1,094 m to 7778 m above sea level at Tirichmir Peak. With its collection
of rugged mountains, gushing rivers, hot springs, and fruit-laden orchards,
Chitral truly is an enchanting part of Pakistan. The area is bordered by
Afghanistan in the north and west, with the narrow Afghan Wakhan corridor
separating it from Tajikistan. Chitral can be accessed via several mountain
passes, the most famous being the Lowari Top (3,118 m) approximately crossing
the Hindu Raj (a spur of the higher Hindukush) in the south and the Shandur
Pass (3,798 m) forming the eastern gateway from Gilgit. Other passes include the
Dorah Pass from Badakhshan in Afghanistan and the Broghil (3,798 m) from the
Wakhan Corridor in Afghanistan. Although these two passes represented the main
arteries of the ancient Silk Route to Yarkand and Kashgar in China and
Badakhshan in Afghanistan, they are not much in use today

destinations.title: Charsadda
destinations.description: The ruins of Balahisar stand 29km to the northeast of Peshawar. One km north of the bridge at Jindi River, Charsadda.From here 5km down towards Takht-i-Bhai is Ghani Dheri Complex, the site of the Pushkalavati Museum. Thakht-i-Bhai town is located 20 km from Ghani Dheri and the Takht-i-Bhai Buddhist monastery is about 3km from the town. Identified by Alexander Cunningham as the first capital of Gandhara in the 19th century and excavated by Sir Mortimer Wheeler in 1958, it remained the first capital of Gandhara under the Achaemenids in the 6th century BC and was invaded by Alexander the Great in 327 BC

destinations.title: Malakand
destinations.description:
Malakand is a District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, offers a mesmerizing blend of natural splendor and historical significance. Its lush valleys, majestic hills, and winding rivers create a captivating backdrop that beckons exploration and awe-inspiring vistas. With a rich historical heritage, Malakand echoes with the whispers of ancient civilizations, bearing testament to its pivotal role as a historic crossroads. Archaeological treasures like Udegram stand as reminders of the district's connection to the Gandhara legacy, while its vibrant Pashtun culture imbues the region with a sense of community and warmth.
 Modern progress flows through Malakand's veins, as its economy thrives on the foundations of agriculture, trade, and emerging industries. Educational institutions, ranging from schools to colleges, play a vital role in shaping intellectual growth, exemplifying the district's commitment to both preserving its history and embracing contemporary development. Amidst its serene natural landscapes, Malakand invites visitors to embark on a journey that bridges the past and the present, immersing them in a district that is at once a custodian of its cultural heritage and a promising canvas for the future.

destinations.title: Karak
destinations.description:
Karak is a district of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province,
Pakistan. It is situated in the south of Kohat District and also share
boundaries with Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Mianwali and Warizistan districts on the
main Indus Highway (NA-55) between Peshawar and Karachi - it is 123 km from the
provincial capital Peshawar. History Until 1940, this whole area was ruled by
the Teri Nawab. Teri was the capital and the only Tehsil. It had tappas
(satrapies): Teri, Seni, Khurram and Barak. Between 1940 and 1982 it was a part
of Kohat, after the July 1, 1982, it has been a separate district. The district
is predominantly populated by Khattak tribe. The series of high and low
mountains of salt range enter into Karak from Punjab. There are large number of
salt mines in Jatta Ismail Khel, Garh jawal khel and Bahadar Khel areas. There
are also large number of mines of Gypsum in Jatta valley and Garh jawal khel.
District Karak is rich in Oil & Gas. The people of Karak are famous for
their hospitality.

destinations.title: Kolai Palas
destinations.description:
Kolai Palas, an alluring district in the embrace of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, unfolds as a realm of natural wonder and cultural mystique. This district's identity is intricately woven into its breathtaking landscapes, where towering peaks, verdant valleys, and dense forests converge to create a visual symphony of beauty. At its heart lies the Kolai Palas valley, a sanctuary of serenity, where time seems to slow down, allowing visitors to escape the bustling world and immerse themselves in nature's tranquility.
 Blessed with an abundance of biodiversity, Kolai Palas district serves as a haven for both flora and fauna. The district's diverse ecosystems provide a refuge for rare and elusive species, including the revered snow leopard and other remarkable wildlife. Amidst the natural grandeur, the local communities have preserved their cultural heritage, adding layers of human history to the district's tapestry. The warm hospitality and unique traditions of the inhabitants offer visitors an opportunity to glimpse into the soul of this enchanting land.

destinations.title: Shangla
destinations.description: A Very Beautiful District Next To Swat With Many Breathtaking Spots For Picnic And A Beautiful Scenery. A Lot Of Snow Fall Happens In Shangla In Winter. The Summer Season Is Normally Very Pleasant With Temperatures Ranging Between 15 To 25 Degrees In Most Places. The Main Places To Look Out For Are Shangla Top (Border Of Swat And Shangla, Yakhtange (Puran), Logay (Ajmir), Bilkanai, Ranyal Dam. Yakhtangay And Logay Are Very Popular Among Tourists For Picnics. Besham Is A Town Situated On The Bank Of Abasin (River Sindh) And Lies Half Way Between Islamabad And Gilgit On The Main Shahrahe Raisham Road Or More Popularly Known As The Silk Route In The World. Besham Is The Hottest Town In Shangla. Further From Besham Comes Dandai Which Is The Border Area Between Shangla And Battagram District. Most Of Shangla Is Covered In Mountains Including Some Very High Peaks.

destinations.title: Chitral Lower
destinations.description:
Lower Chitral had a sex ratio of 937 females per 1000
males and a literacy rate of 63.00% - 75.71% for males and 49.37% for females.
49,780 (17.89%) lived in urban areas. 27.10% of the population was under 10
years of age. 3,902 (1.40%) were from religious minorities, almost all of whom
are followers of the indigenous animistic Kalash faith that was once the
dominant faith in the district before the spread of Islam.
 89.48% of the population spoke languages recorded as 'Other'
on the census. Most of these spoke Khowar (or
Chitrali), the dominant language of Chitral as a whole. A minority spoke Chitral Kalasha and Wakhi ,
with the Kalasha dominating several valleys and the Wakhis spread
throughout the north of the district near the Afghan border. Pashto is
spoken in the southeast of the district by 9.11% of the population. There
are some speakers of the Madaklasht dialect , a Persian
dialect which is considered a mix of Dari and Tajik .
 Lower Chitral covers the area from lowari to Barenis and
Gobor in the Garam Chashma side.
 The unique culture of Chitral, developed over many millennia
with more than a dozen ethnic groups speaking as many languages, is closely
linked to that of Central Asia and China instead of South Asia, according to a
study conducted by International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
 It says that arts and crafts, traditional costumes, food and
beverages, local games, music, dance, folksongs and legendary sites form the
main components of the cultural heritage of Chitral. The study also includes
the historic military sites and indigenous tribes (Kalash) in the ingredients
of cultural heritage.
 “Chitral's artisans manufacture a wide range of elegant and
delicately crafted jewellery, woodwork and embroidery, woven and knitted
textiles,” the study says, adding that clay, wood, stone, bone, animal skin and
copper are the material most commonly used.
 The woolen fabric of Chitral, locally called shu, and
walnut-wood furniture are popular in handicraft markets throughout the country.
 The study adds that traditional clothes, including that of
Kalash people, are made from wool and silk and decorated with beads and shells.
 Traditional cap, (khapol) and gown (chugha) are popular
while the typical Chitrali shoes (khon) resemble the long riding boots.
 The area's vast culinary repertoire of foods and beverages
is unique in terms of both flavour and presentation.
 The study places music and dance at the heart of Chitrali
culture. Chitral's rich and varied musical tradition is part of the fabric of
everyday life while Chitrali sitar is famous throughout the world and the
traditional dances, such as dani and sauz are part of the folk heritage of
Central Asia.
 The folk poets of Chitral sing war songs as well as love
ballades, the study says, adding that epics are popular among the Kalash.
 “With its origin lost in the mists of antiquity, the ancient
tribe of Kalash is a unique cultural resource,” says the study, adding that
Chilm Jusht, Uchhal, Chitirmas are some of the main festivals of the tribe that
attract a large number of tourists to the three segregated valleys of Bumburate,
Birir and Rumbur in Chitral

destinations.title: Orakzai
destinations.description:
Orakzai emerges as a district of distinct character and historical significance. Set against a backdrop of rugged terrain and picturesque landscapes, this land holds stories that have weathered the test of time. Bordered by neighboring regions and embracing a rich tribal heritage, Orakzai encapsulates a blend of tradition and modernity.
 The district's landscape, a harmonious interplay of valleys and hills, tells tales of resilience and adaptation. Amidst these natural contours, the people of Orakzai have carved out their existence, maintaining cultural traditions while forging pathways toward progress. The region's tribal dynamics and historical evolution have woven a narrative that reflects the spirit of its inhabitants.
 As sunlight filters through the valleys and casts shadows on the ridges, Orakzai stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of its communities. It beckons those seeking to uncover its hidden treasures and engage with its hospitable residents, inviting a deeper understanding of the interplay between tradition and modernity in this captivating district.

destinations.title: Nowshera
destinations.description: Nowshera is a district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa near Peshawar, seamlessly marries tradition with progress. Its cultural tapestry, rich in Pashtun heritage, comes alive through vibrant festivals and traditional crafts that reflect the district's sense of community. Nowshera's strategic location fuels its economic vitality, with a thriving industrial landscape contributing to local employment and national economic growth. Amidst bustling markets and trade, Nowshera's educational institutions nurture intellectual growth, fostering a generation of thinkers and professionals. The district's natural beauty, including the scenic River Kabul, offers a serene escape, complementing its efforts toward sustainable development and improved civic amenities. In Nowshera, the past and present harmoniously converge, inviting travelers and enthusiasts to explore its dynamic blend of culture, commerce, and natural charm.

destinations.title: Dera Ismail Khan
destinations.description:
This is one of the biggest and most important cities of the Southern
region of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Situated on the Western bank of the Indus River, the
old city used to be surrounded by a mud wall having ten gates. Some of the gates
are know as Imaman Wala, Topanwala, Thatharanwala and Powindah Seraiwala. The city
is a trading center and famous for wood and embroidery works. The city was
founded by Malik Suhail Baloch in the 15th century AD and he named it after one of
his son.

destinations.title: Battagram
destinations.description: The District Battagram Is Surrounded By Kohistan District To The North, Mansehra District To The East, Kala Dhaka Tribal Area To The South And Shangla District To The West. Its Headquarter Is At Battagram Town At A Distance Of About 75 Km From Mansehra On The Silk Highway. The District Consists Of Two Tehsils, Battagram And Allai. It Has A Number Of Beautiful Valleys And The District Covers An Area Of 350,172 Acres. The District Is Mostly Mountainous With Peaks Rising Above 4000 Meters With Thick Forests. However, Fertile Plain Areas Exist In Nindhyar, Tijri Deshan, Batamori, Banna And Rashang Valleys. Plenty Of Springs And Streams Flow Through Out The District, Providing Water For Drinking And Irrigation. There Are Two Main Streams (Locally Called Khawar) I.E. The Nindhyar Khawar And Allai Khawar. Nindhyar Khawar Originates In The Mountains Of “Hill” And After Flowing Through The Main Village Joins Indus River At Thakot In The East. The Other Big Stream, The Allai Khawar Originates In Chaur Mountains And Joins The Indus River At Kund In The East. The Climate In Battagram Is Moderate In Summer And Severe Cold In Winter. Upper Parts Of The District Especially Shamlai, Hill And Bilandkot Of Battagram Tehsil And Sorgai, Rashand, Gangwal, Bateela And Pashto Batangi Of Allai Tehsil Receive Heavy Snowfall. Chaur Is Snowbound And Inaccessible For Eight Months In The Year.

destinations.title: Kohat
destinations.description:
Kohat was founded by Raja Kohat in the 4th century BC. It
saw many ups and downs in history. The Sikh built a fort here, which was
modified by the British and stands magnificently in the heart of the town. On
one side of the fort are the famous Jangal Khel springs, with banyan trees
around. Just outside the fort are a boulder, well and vhill-gah (meditation
place) associated with Hazrat Syed Abdullah Haji Bahadar Kohati (RA). He lived
in the times of Aurangzeb Alamgir and his shrine is located inside the city.
There is also a grand mosque near the shrine. The shrine of another Holy man
Hazrat Bona Pir (RA) is situated north of Kohat at the foot of the hills
and is visible from miles away. There is also a perennial spring near the
shrine.

destinations.title: Kohistan
destinations.description:
Kohistan District, situated within the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, is a district of captivating contrasts that encapsulates both rugged natural beauty and a rich cultural heritage. The district's diverse topography encompasses majestic mountains, fertile valleys, and meandering rivers, creating a picturesque landscape that beckons nature enthusiasts and adventurers. Kohistan's geographical composition lends itself to outdoor exploration, offering hiking trails, stunning vistas, and a serene environment that resonates with both locals and visitors.
 Steeped in history, Kohistan holds echoes of ancient civilizations and trade routes, shaping its cultural tapestry. The district's communities are infused with traditions, customs, and craftsmanship that bear the marks of its historical interactions. The warmth of its people and their genuine hospitality reflect a sense of unity and shared identity. As Kohistan embraces progress, it strives to maintain its unique character, fostering a balance between preserving its cultural roots and embracing modern developments. In essence, Kohistan is an invitation to delve into a land where nature's splendor and historical legacy converge, creating a destination that offers a glimpse into the heart of a captivating district within Pakistan.

destinations.title: Lakki Marwat
destinations.description:
The town of Lakki was founded as Ihsanpur by Fateh Khan Tiwana in 1844.
The town was shi ft ed to its present
location in 1864. It derives its present name from Diwan Lakki Mal of the
Sikhs. It is an important trading center and headquarter of District Lakki
Marwat. The population comprises mainly of Marwats and also includes Mina Khel,
Khoidad Khel and Syed Khel.

destinations.title: Buner
destinations.description:
Buner District, cradled within the embrace of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is a captivating realm where history, nature, and culture converge harmoniously. Its picturesque landscape, adorned with rolling hills, lush valleys, and meandering rivers, creates an enchanting tableau that beckons both locals and visitors alike. Rich in heritage, Buner reveals its ancient secrets through landmarks like the Takht Bhai Buddhist monastery, a testament to its historical significance along the ancient Silk Road. This district is a canvas painted with the vibrant hues of Pashtun traditions, where intricate embroidery, traditional attire, and spirited folk music flourish, fostering a strong sense of community and warmth among its residents.
 Buner's heartbeat resonates with agrarian rhythms, as terraced fields yield bountiful crops like wheat, maize, and fruits, sustaining the livelihoods of its inhabitants. As Buner embraces modernity while cherishing its roots, it holds promise for sustainable growth and responsible tourism. The district's allure lies not only in its breathtaking landscapes and historical treasures but also in its commitment to preserving its cultural heritage and natural splendor, ensuring that Buner remains a captivating destination that bridges the past with the aspirations of the future.

destinations.title: Bannu
destinations.description:
Bannu is and old town west of the Tochi Vally. The old town
was surrounded by a high mud wall, having gates in all directions. The Sikhs
built a fort here, which was named as Dilip Garh or Dilip Nagar after Maharajah
Dilip Singh. This is the biggest Sikh fort in the frontier, with mud walls and
bastions. The British had named the town as Edwards Abad and a British Cemetery
exists in the Cantonment are. The Airport known as Islam Bibi Airport was named
after the Hindu girl, who converted to Islam in the mid-1930s. The ancient site
of Akra is located in the district.

destinations.title: Hangu
destinations.description:
Hangu District, situated at the heart of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, offers a captivating blend of historical significance and tranquil landscapes. Its diverse terrain, characterized by rolling hills and fertile plains, creates a picturesque backdrop that beckons exploration and contemplation. Hangu's rich Pashtun traditions contribute to a sense of warmth and community, making it a destination that embraces both its history and the promise of modern development.
 Hangu's commitment to progress is reflected in its higher educational institutions, which play a pivotal role in nurturing intellectual growth. These institutes contribute to the district's intellectual landscape, empowering a generation of thinkers and professionals. As Hangu strides forward, its economy thrives through agriculture, commerce, and emerging small-scale industries. Amidst its serene natural beauty, Hangu stands as an inviting haven, where visitors can immerse themselves in a district that harmonizes the echoes of its past with the aspirations of a vibrant future, while education remains a cornerstone of its evolving identity.

destinations.title: Tank
destinations.description:
The town of Tank is about 65 kilometers away
from Dera Ismail Khan. This big trading center has a large ruined mud fort
constructed by Sarwar Khan in the early 19th century AD. Sir Henry Durand, the
lieutenant Governor of the then Punjab Province was killed here in 1870 while
sitting on an elephant and trying to pass through one of the gateways.

destinations.title: Torghar
destinations.description:
Torghar is a district located within the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. Nestled amidst the picturesque landscapes of the country, Tor Ghar is renowned for its breathtaking natural beauty and its significance in the local cultural and historical context.
 The Tor Ghar region is characterized by its towering peaks, deep valleys, and diverse ecosystems. Its name "Tor Ghar" translates to "Black Mountain," which aptly describes the dark, rocky terrain that dominates the landscape. The mountains are known for their strategic location and have played a role in the region's history, with ancient forts and remnants serving as a testament to their historical importance.
 Despite its challenging topography, Tor Ghar is inhabited by resilient communities that have thrived amidst the harsh conditions. The people of Tor Ghar have a unique way of life, deeply rooted in tradition, and their cultural practices have stood the test of time.

destinations.title: Khyber
destinations.description:
District Khyber, nestled within the Peshawar Division of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan, stands as a testament to the region's evolving administrative landscape. Formerly designated as an agency within the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA), this district experienced a significant transformation in 2018. With the momentous merger of FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, District Khyber emerged as an integral and distinct entity within the provincial framework.
 This transition marked a historic shift in governance, elevating Khyber from its previous agency status to a formal district structure. This evolution unlocked new avenues for development, local governance, and representation, aligning the district with the dynamic political and administrative landscape of Pakistan.
 Encompassing a diverse geographical expanse, District Khyber stretches from the captivating Tirah valley to the bustling city of Peshawar. This range of landscapes reflects the district's unique blend of natural beauty, cultural heritage, and strategic significance. Khyber's journey embodies the nation's commitment to unity and cohesion, exemplifying a broader vision of inclusive governance and regional integration.

destinations.title: Kurram
destinations.description: Kurram District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, In the northeastern reaches lies the Afghan province of Nangarhar, featuring iconic landmarks such as the renowned Tora Bora and the majestic Koh-E-Safed. Koh-E-Safed's lofty mountain ranges, annually adorned with a snow-white blanket, emerge as a natural geographical boundary between Afghanistan and Pakistan, their towering presence shaping a distinct border. To the west, the Afghan province of Paktia extends its embrace, intricately weaving connections with Kurram District, while to the south, the district of Khost completes this interplay of proximity. Meanwhile, the eastern edge of Kurram converges harmoniously with Tull in Pakistan's Hangu District, forming a dynamic nexus of cross-border interactions and cultural entwinement. In Kurram, mountains and narratives converge, forging a compelling tale of geographical divisions and human connections.

destinations.title: Mohmand
destinations.description:
Mohmand District, encompassing an area of 2296 square kilometers, is home to a population of approximately 466,944. This district, while relatively compact in size, holds significant importance. Agriculture and minerals stand as its prominent sectors, shaping the local economy and livelihoods. Despite its potential, the cultivated area accounts for only about 9% of the total land, reflecting the challenges of limited arable land.
 Water scarcity poses a significant concern across various parts of the district, underscoring the need for sustainable water management strategies. Amidst these challenges, agriculture remains a vital contributor, with vegetables taking center stage among its predominant products. These crops not only sustain local communities but also serve as a source of trade and commerce.

destinations.title: South Waziristan
destinations.description:
South Waziristan is a district in Dera Ismail Khan division
in the rugged heart of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, South Waziristan
stands as a region of captivating contrasts and historical significance.
Bordered by neighboring districts and Afghanistan, this land bears witness to a
rich tapestry of cultures and histories. The region's undulating landscapes,
characterized by arid plains, lush valleys, and jagged peaks, tell stories of
resilience and adaptability.
 South Waziristan's history is deeply intertwined with its
tribal heritage, where traditions have thrived for generations. The region's
complex social fabric has witnessed shifts and transformations, playing host to
diverse communities that have shaped its identity. The towering Shawal and Spin
Ghar mountain ranges from natural barriers, revealing the district's unique
topography and offering a vivid portrayal of the challenges and opportunities
that define life here.

destinations.title: North Waziristan
destinations.description:
The North Waziristan borders in the
north with Kurram and Kohat, in the east with Kohat and Bannu, in the south
with the South Waziristan and in the west with Afghanistan. The district is the
second largest in previous FATA, with an area of 4,707 square kilometers.
 The district presents huge potential
in mining sector as huge reserves of copper has been identified while Chromite,
Manganese reserves are also available. Furthermore, oil and gas reserves are
also being explored by KPOGCL and it is expected to add towards growth of North
Waziristan in near future. Miran Exploration Block is located in North
Waziristan and Kurram agency. Investment opportunities for local and foreign
companies in E&P are available via joint venture.
 South and North Waziristan are both
highest producers of pine nuts (Chalghoza) and Pakistan is reported to be the
second highest exporter of pine nuts after China. However, due to lack of
training in harvesting, cutting, roasting and processing there is high
percentage of wastage. Value addition in pine nut handling is strongly
recommended.

destinations.title: Bajaur
destinations.description:
District Bajaur, situated within the Malakand Division of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in Pakistan, holds a distinctive position in the region's administrative landscape. Previously designated as an agency of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA), this district underwent a significant transformation in 2018. With the historic merger of FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Bajaur emerged as a distinct and integral district within the province.
This transition marked a pivotal moment in Bajaur's governance, as it shifted from its previous administrative framework to the formal structure of a district. This change brought about new opportunities for development, local governance, and representation, aligning the region with the evolving political and administrative landscape of Pakistan.
Bajaur's history and geography contribute to its unique character, as it continues to navigate the path of progress within the larger framework of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The district's journey exemplifies the nation's commitment to unity and integration, reflecting a broader vision of inclusive governance and regional cohesion.

destinations.title: Astore Tourist Destinations
destinations.description:
GOVERNMENT OF GILGIT BALTISTAN 
                                Tourism, Sports, Culture, Archaeology & Museums Department

Astore District is one of the ten districts in Gilgit−Baltistan, with its administrative centers located in Eidgah and Gorikot. To the north, it borders Gilgit District, while Roundu District lies to the northeast, and Skardu District to the east. To the southeast is Kharmang District, and to the west is Diamer District. The stunning blue colors of this beautiful Attabad Lake, nestled among the peaks of the Karakoram mountain range in Gilgit Baltistan Northern Areas of Pakistan, belies its violent origin. Attabad Lake is known as one of the most beautiful lakes in the Gilgit Baltistan region of Pakistan, attracting thousands of tourists every year. The architecture of Khaplu Palace is a fusion of Himalayan, Kashmiri and Mughal styles, in terms of its spatial organization and overall decoration. The spaces inside the palace provide a historical record of the raja's lifestyle. attractions.title: Minar-e-Pakistan
attractions.description:
Minar-e-Pakistan is a national monument located in Lahore’s Greater Iqbal Park, built between 1960 and 1968 to commemorate the 1940 Lahore Resolution—the first formal call for a separate homeland for the Muslims of British India. Designed by architect Nasreddin Murat-Khan, it has become one of Pakistan’s most iconic symbols of nationhood and independence.

Key facts
Location: Iqbal Park, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan

Height: ~70 meters (230 feet)

Construction: 1960–1968

Architect: Nasreddin Murat-Khan

Purpose: Commemorates the 1940 Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution

Historical significance
The Minar marks the site where the All-India Muslim League passed the Lahore Resolution on March 23, 1940, an event that laid the ideological foundation for Pakistan’s creation in 1947. The monument was commissioned under President Ayub Khan to enshrine that political milestone in stone and serve as a national reminder of the struggle for independence.

Architecture and symbolism
The tower blends Mughal, Islamic, and modern design influences. Rising from a star-shaped base, its four platforms—made from rough stone, chiseled stone, polished stone, and white marble—symbolize stages of the Muslims’ struggle, from oppression to independence. Inscriptions on marble tablets include Quranic verses, the 99 names of Allah, the national anthem, and speeches by Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal in multiple languages.

Cultural and political role
Beyond its historic value, Minar-e-Pakistan remains a central stage for political gatherings, national celebrations, and civic demonstrations. Major parties—including Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz), Pakistan Peoples Party, and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf—have held mass rallies here, underlining its enduring symbolic link between political aspiration and popular will.

Present setting
Encircled by the landscaped Greater Iqbal Park, the Minar overlooks Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort. The park includes gardens, fountains, and a lake, making the monument both a historical landmark and a popular recreation site for residents and visitors alike.

attractions.title: Lahore Museum
attractions.description:
The Lahore Museum is a major cultural and historical museum located on Mall Road, Pakistan. Established in 1865 and reopened in 1894 in its current Indo-Saracenic red-brick building, it is among the oldest and most visited museums in South Asia. It preserves a vast collection of artifacts spanning prehistoric, Buddhist, Islamic, Sikh, and colonial eras, reflecting the subcontinent’s rich heritage.

Key facts
Founded: 1865 (moved to current site 1894)

Location: Mall Road, Anarkali, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan

Architectural style: Indo-Saracenic (Mughal–British fusion)

Notable exhibit: Fasting Buddha (Gandhara period)

Visiting hours: 9 a.m.–3:30 p.m., closed Fridays

History and Architecture
Originally called the “Central Museum,” it was established during British colonial rule and designed in the Indo-Saracenic style that blends Mughal domes and arches with Victorian elements. The Zamzama Gun, famously featured in Kim, stands at its entrance. The museum building itself, protected under Punjab’s Special Premises Ordinance, remains a landmark of late-19th-century civic architecture.

Collections and Galleries
The museum holds more than 20 galleries displaying objects from the Indus Valley Civilization to the modern era. Highlights include Greco-Buddhist sculptures from Gandhara, Mughal and Pahari miniature paintings, Islamic manuscripts and calligraphy, arms, coins, ethnographic displays, and colonial-era artifacts. The Fasting Buddha, carved from schist, is one of its most celebrated pieces.

Cultural Significance
As Pakistan’s premier repository of art and archaeology, the Lahore Museum illustrates the region’s religious and artistic diversity—housing Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh, and Islamic relics side by side. It serves as an educational hub for scholars and visitors alike, offering insight into South Asia’s complex cultural continuum.

Visitor Information
Located centrally near the National College of Arts, the museum is accessible by public transport. Admission fees are modest—approximately PKR 50 for locals and PKR 1,000 for foreign nationals. Most visitors spend two to three hours exploring its exhibits.

attractions.title: Wagah Border
attractions.description:
The Wagah Border is a ceremonial and operational border crossing between India and Pakistan, located between Amritsar in Indian Punjab and Lahore in Pakistani Punjab. It is famed for its daily flag-lowering ceremony that symbolizes both rivalry and cooperation between the two nations.

Key facts
Location: Between Amritsar, India, and Lahore, Pakistan

Opened: 1947, after Partition of British India

Primary crossing: Between India’s Amritsar and Pakistan’s Lahore

Ceremony start: 1959

Main participants: Border Security Force and Pakistan Rangers

Historical background
Established following the 1947 Partition, the Wagah Border became one of the key gateways for migration and later for controlled cross-border trade. It sits on the Grand Trunk Road, historically a major route connecting South and Central Asia. The border gained symbolic significance as a site representing the geopolitical division and shared heritage of India and Pakistan.

The Beating Retreat ceremony
Every evening before sunset, both countries’ forces perform the “Beating Retreat” or flag-lowering ceremony. This synchronized parade features elaborate marching, high kicks, and nationalistic displays. The ceremony, often attended by hundreds of spectators on each side, has become a popular patriotic and tourist event, symbolizing both tension and respect.

Tourism and infrastructure
The Indian side, known as the Attari–Wagah Border, includes large spectator stands and visitor facilities. It is managed by the Border Security Force, which coordinates crowd control and ceremonial arrangements. Visitors require valid identification, and the event remains one of the top tourist attractions in Amritsar, drawing both domestic and international audiences.

Symbolism and significance
The Wagah Border stands as a daily reminder of the complex relationship between India and Pakistan—marked by historical conflict yet shared culture. The ceremony’s disciplined choreography and mutual salutes convey coexistence amid rivalry, turning the border into a rare space of ritualized diplomacy.

Quaid-e-Azam who became lifelong honorary member of the Khyber Union ICP in 1936 made the College one of the heirs of his property in 1939. The Quaid Trust later on paid an amount of Rs.1, 08, 11, 600 /- in different installments to the College.

Being the home town of Kohistani inhabitants, Kalam is like an earthly
paradise in Swat Valley. Located at a distance of 40 km from Bahrain, Kalam is the main town of this region presenting one of the
most panoramic natural beauties. The people known as Kohistani are its original inhabitants, proud of their own
language and still unchanged traditions. A fascinating view of 5,957m Falak sar Peak with its melting snow during summers from
Matiltan (3000m) is breathtaking. The journey is incomplete without seeing and going to Mahodand, a famous lake, about 23
km beyond Matiltan. The picturesque Kalam provides road access to reach magnificent valleys of Ushu (2286m) Utror (2225m) and Gabral (2286m) above sea level, where journey through green forests and beautiful view of landscape is
memorising. Rivers and lakes at Kalam offer good trout fishing after getting permits obtainable from the Fisheries
Department.

attractions.title: Shinkiari Hut
attractions.description: Shinkiari Hut - 2 hours from main entrance of road near Shogran and 3 hours from Makra Peak lies on top of the mountain is this beautiful meadow.

attractions.title: Nathia Gali
attractions.description: Nathiagali is a mountainous area and one of the largest hill stations of the country. The atmosphere is very peaceful and the climate of the valley is very pleasant and cool during the summer. You can travel to Nathiagali from Abbottabad or from Murree. Good roads, easy to drive through and you can view lots of landscapes on the way. Many hotels and resorts are available. Families book their resorts in advance and spend the whole summer season in these resorts. You can enjoy hiking, trekking, bird watching, wildlife, and lots of awesome scenery. Nathiagali clad in pine, walnut, oak and maple trees, is the prettiest hill resort in the Galiyat region. It can be approached both from Murree and Abbottabad. It is 38 km from Abbottabad as well as from Murree. Nathiagali is 2501 meters above sea level and is surrounded by lofty mountains. The British tried to create a little England here with its small timbered churches, parks, bungalows, and the Governor's House. Breathtaking landscapes, spring water and fresh air make it one of the most peaceful hill stations in Pakistan.

attractions.title: Kaghan Valley
attractions.description:
Kaghan is a jewel among the many beautiful valleys in
Mansehra District Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. This 160-kilometer-long valley
is most popular for summer holidays with both Pakistanis as well as foreigners. The
valley features pine forests, green meadows, crystal clear lakes, streams.
Kunhar River and snow-covered peaks are the main feature of the valley. Kaghan
is also famous for trout fishing among trout anglers as well as tourists.
Nestled along the banks of the river are the towns of Balakot, Paras,
Mahandari, Kaghan, and Naran. The local people are friendly and simple. Gujar
nomads are one of the most interesting features of the Kaghan Valley. They take
their herds of cattle to the high pastures of the upper Kaghan Valley in spring
and bring them down again in autumn. While going to Kaghan you will find them
camped along the road in their traditional tents or moving up and down the
valley with their herd of sheep and goats.

attractions.title: Jahaz Banda
attractions.description: Upper Dir, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan The long and steep hike of 3-4 hours is worth it, when you see the beautiful view at top of the meadow. Even the hiking track is mesmerizing enough to leave you in wonder. Camping and bonfire are the best activities to do here. You can visit katora lake and another waterfall during your stay here.

attractions.title: Swat Museum
attractions.description:
This museum has a huge and precious collection of Gandhara
Art. Artifacts, stupas, coins of various ages, and other assets of the Gandahara
civilization signify the rich cultural and historical past of the valley. The
museum is situated on the main Mingora- Saidu Sharif road. These artifacts,
antiques, and similar articles are categorized and beautifully showcased. The cultural life of the near past of the valley is displayed in the shape of local
dresses, embroidery, Jewelry, musical instruments, weapons of old times, and carved
Wooden articles. The museum is closed on Friday.

attractions.title: Aansoo Lake
attractions.description: Ansoo Lake is one of the panoramic & beautiful lakes of Pakistan. It is located near Malika Parbat in the Himalayan range in Kaghan Valley. The name “Ansoo” comes from its tear-like shape (the Urdu word Ansoo means teardrop). The lake is said to have been discovered in 1993 by Pakistan Air Force pilots who were flying at a relatively low altitude over the area. Earlier, the lake was not even known to the locals. It can be reached by a difficult trek from Saif-Ul-Muluk Lake, Naran.

attractions.title: Ayubia
attractions.description: A cluster of four small hill stations of Khanaspur, Khairagali, Changlagali, and Ghora Dhaka is called Ayubia. It was named after President Ayub Khan who belonged to the Haripur district of Hazara. Ayubia is spread over an area of 26 km. The central place of Ghora Dhaka has a chairlift, which gives a panoramic and mesmerizing view of the surroundings.

attractions.title: Gor Khatri
attractions.description: The archaeological complex of Gor Khatri was once a Mughal Caravan Serai crowning the hill at the top end of Sethi Street. Huge Mughal gateways on either end lead into a large courtyard, over 200 meters square, that was once surrounded on all four sides by rooms for travelers. The site has been considered holy for more than 2,000 years. In the second century AD, it was a Buddhist shrine and monastery known as the Tower of the Buddhas Bowl Remains of a temple to Gorakhnath, a yogi sect, stands in the southeastern corner of the courtyard, with a shrine to Nandi beside it. An archaeological dig in the northeastern corner of Gor Khatri has established that Peshawar is one of the earliest living cities in this part of Asia, inhabited continuously from the 4 to 6th century BC when it was a province of the Persian Achaemenian Empire. From then onwards, it was ruled in turn by the Mauryans, Greeks, Scythians, Kushans, Sasanians, White Huns, Hindu Shahis, Ghaznavids, Ghorids, Suri Afghans, Mughals, Durrani Afghans, Sikhs, and the British, before becoming Pakistan in 1947.

attractions.title: University Road
attractions.description: University Road is a commercial and residential area in Peshawar and is one of the busiest roads in the city. It starts from the historic Qissa Khawani Bazaar and runs to the University of Peshawar. The road is a major route for traffic travelling to and from Hayatabad and the Ring Road. It is also home to several educational institutions, including the University of Peshawar.

attractions.title: Mabali Island
attractions.description: Khanpur road , Haripur , Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

attractions.title: Gahanta ghar
attractions.description: The Cunningham Clock Tower (Urdu: ‎کننگہام گھنٹہ گھر‎) in Peshawar, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, was built in 1900, in commemoration of the Diamond Jubilee of Her Majesty the Queen Empress". The tower was named after Sir George Cunningham, former British governor and political agent in the province.

attractions.title: Madyan
attractions.description:
The valley of Madyan is situated about 56 kilometers to the
north of Mingora (Pr: Mingawara) city. It lies on the main road that leads to
Bahrain, Kalam, and other beautiful valleys of Swat. Its riverside location and
cool climate make it an
 attractive spot with rows of shops, hotels, and
restaurants queued along the road. The trout farms and restaurant adds to its
fascination. Local handicrafts, embroidery, and antiques are displayed at
roadside shops. The slightly wider valley of Madyan is different in comparison
to other valleys in the sense that almost every type of modern facility and
amenity is available here i.e. internet, cellular networks, cable and satellite
TV, hotels, restaurants, and other basic necessities of life. Apart from these up to-date facilities, tall mountains covered with green foliage and dotted with small mud and concrete houses from three sides surround the beautiful town of Madyan. The roaring and foaming river Swat looks like a ferocious monster here as the huge mountains on both sides appear to fetter and restrain its movement.

attractions.title: Takht-i-bahi Buddhist Monastery
attractions.description: Takht-i-Bahi is an archaeological site in Mardan , Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The Buddhist ruins of Takhat-Bahi are a monastic complex, founded in the early 1st century AD. The ruins include a central stupa court, the Votive Stupas Court, a group of three stupas, a monastery square meditation cell, a conference hall, and covered footpaths. The unique stupa and monastic site of Takht-i-Bahi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The relics recovered from here are exhibited in the Peshawar Museum. On the main Malakan Swat road and heading towards the north one reaches Chakdara Bridge, where the famous Churchill’s Piqued can also be seen.

attractions.title: Peochar Valley
attractions.description: Peochar valley is located about 41 km from Mingora city. It's a worth seeing place for tourists. Lush green mountains and beautiful forests. It's 6000 feet in height from sea level. Tucked away in the picturesque Swat Valley, Peochar Valley is a haven of natural beauty. The valley is renowned for its lush green meadows, towering mountains, and glistening streams. It offers a peaceful and serene environment, perfect for those seeking tranquility and solace. The valley is a paradise for adventure enthusiasts, offering opportunities for hiking, trekking, and camping amidst the breathtaking landscape. The vibrant colors of wildflowers in the spring and the snowy peaks in the winter make Peochar Valley a year-round destination. The locals, known for their warm hospitality, add to the charm of the place. A visit to Peochar Valley in Swat is a chance to immerse yourself in nature’s wonders and create unforgettable memories.

attractions.title: Shogran
attractions.description: Shogran, one of the most beautiful plateaus in the valley, is situated 34 kilometers from Balakot via Kewai. To reach this quaint place, take a side road on the right after passing through Kewai. From here it is a steep 7 kilometers to Shogran. The road is metalled and normal cars and vans can make the drive. Surrounded by thick pine forests and with an altitude of 7747 feet, the summer climate of Shogran is very mild and pleasant. One of the nicer places to visit is Shogran's Forest Rest House. From the rolling grassy lawns of the rest house, one can see breathtaking panoramic views of snow covered mountains. Kaghan Valley's highest peaks, such as Musa Ka Musalla (4419 m), Makra (3885 m) and Malika Parbat (5290 m), are visible from here. For those wishing to stay for the night or have a meal, there are a number of small and medium-sized hotels in Shogran. For more information on hotels please consult the list of hotels.

attractions.title: Shingrayi Waterfall
attractions.description:
Shingrayi waterfall is situated in the vicinity of Shingrayi
village near Manglor. It is one of the most famous waterfalls in Swat. Due to
its easy excess and charming beauty, it is highly attractive spot for
domestic tourist. Tourist are advised to use 4x4 vehicles as the rout from
Shingrayi village until the waterfall (about 40 minutes) can only be accessed
either by foot, motorbikes or 4x4 vehicles. The scenery on the way is superb
and people can enjoy a high-altitude view of almost the whole district Swat.
The series of mountainous chain from Buner to Shangla appears at a glance and
the sunset between them is one of a magical experience.

attractions.title: Dashti Laila Swat
attractions.description:
Located in the beautiful Swat Valley of
Pakistan, Dasht-e-Laila is one of the most popular tourist spots in the
country, offering a picturesque view of its surroundings and many things to do.
With dense forests, numerous lakes and rivers, and snow-capped mountains, it
provides an excellent destination for vacationers This is a natural
attraction located in Swat, Pakistan. It is a large open valley
covered in a blanket of wildflowers. The best time to visit is spring when the
flowers bloom. The valley is a popular hiking destination; several trails wind
through the flowers.

attractions.title: Baghicha Family Park
attractions.description: Fazalabad, Charsadda, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan Contact : +923189020009

attractions.title: Mingora
attractions.description: Mingora (Pr: Mingawara) the center of economic activities and the only urban area of the valley is adjacent to Saidu Sharif. It offers traditional, Pakistani and Western food outlets, restaurants and hotels. Locally produced beautifully displayed at its main bazaar, shops, show rooms etc. include semi-precious stones, embroider dresses, hand woven ladies’ shawls, bed, sheets and woodwork. Traditional ornaments and antiques are available at shops. Visitors on trips to Swat valley usually stroll in its bazaars for shopping at the end of their journey. You can find emerald mines in hills northward of the city, famous worldwide for their expensive and valuable emeralds.

attractions.title: Bishigram
attractions.description:
The sprawling valley of Bishigram is
the last village on the road. The houses are built like gigantic steps on the uneven
landscape of the mountain. The total time to reach the valley from Madyan is forty minutes
as the road is not in good condition. Several other small hamlets surround the valley,
which can be approached by trekking for an hour and a half. The track to Bishigram
Lake starts from this village and that is how it has taken its name. Lush green forests
surround the valley, which receives heavy snowfall. Several springs and streams are
scattered throughout the valley. Electricity and telephone facilities are
available. The area is no more secluded and the people visit the nearby town of
Madyan almost on daily basis to merchandise their goods and buy the daily
consumable items. Most of the inhabitants live permanently here while the
adjoining hamlets are deserted during winter and are occupied in the summer
again.

attractions.title: Miandam
attractions.description: The Miandam Swat Pakistan is on a hillside, with small terraced fields and houses with beehives in the walls. It is a good place for walking, with paths along the stream. Miandam is a picturesque town that offers breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. With its mild climate and abundant natural beauty, it is a popular tourist destination for those looking to escape the lowlands’ heat and experience the mountains’ tranquility. The distance from Mingora to Miandam is approximately 50.7 kilometers (31 miles), and the estimated travel time by car is 1 hour and 49 minutes via Bagh Deri Road. This route passes through the city of Bagh Deri and offers panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys.

attractions.title: Daral Lake
attractions.description: The Daral Lake is located northeast of Saidgai Lake and can be reached by a challenging trek of two to three hours from Saidgai. Daral has a trail full of fun and amusement, since it passes through mountains with sky-touching heights that provide spectacular views. An alternative route also leads to Daral Lake, which is a 6-hour trek from Gabeen Jabba. There are beautiful meadows surrounding Daral Lake. The lake is open from May through September. The Daral River flows from this lake through a small stream. The dense forests of conifers, pines, and cedars that cover the deep canyon at Bahrain Valley provide shelter from the intense sun as you descend. If you are an expert of herbal plants, you will find countless treasures of herbal plants.

attractions.title: Chukail meadows
attractions.description:
Chukail Banda (meadows) is located in the north of Mankial valley. Surrounded by picturesque summer pastures, these highlands have become a hot favourite travel destination for many tourists. The glorious peaks of Mankial overshadow the green pastures and give an impression of protecting the valleys from bad omens.
Chukail meadows are home to the famous endangered Markhor, Snow leopards, wolves, Golden monal, Black bear and many other wild animal species and the valley is declared a national park by the government of Pakistan. This unique trek to Chukail meadows to give an exciting opportunity for nature lovers to witness the enchanting hidden beauty of Swat valley.

attractions.title: Zamung park
attractions.description:
Zamung Park or Zamung Mega Park located in Mardan District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The park was completed in December 2022. The park has water slides, a children’s play area, an electronic dinosaur, and other facilities in the 400-Kanal area.
 Park entry ticket for children's above age 05 yrs is Rs 150/- per child.
 Park entry ticket for adults is Rs 250/- per person.
 Park entry ticket for children's below age 05 yrs is exempted.
 Park opening time is 10:00 AM.
 Park closing time is 10:00 PM.

attractions.title: Kalash Valley
attractions.description:
The Kalash valleys of Chitral are located in the southern
gorges of the Hindu Kush mountain range in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Province. The valleys share a 380 km border with Afghanistan in the north &
west, and the Central Asian states of Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kirghizstan
are easily accessible from the area. To the east lies Gilgit, from where one
can reach China's Xinjiang Autonomous Region along the legendary Karakoram
Highway. There are three theories about the origin of the Kalash. Some
historians believe that the Kalash are descendants of the soldiers of Alexander
the Great, while the second group believes that they are indigenous to Asia and
came from what is now the Nuristan area of Afghanistan, According to the third
school of thought; the Kalash ancestors migrated to Afghanistan from a distant
place in South Asia, which they call "Tsiyam" in their folk songs and
epics. However, it is established that the Kalash migrated to Chitral from
Afghanistan in the 2nd century B.C. By the 10th century AD., the Kalash ruled a
large part of present-day Chitral. Razhawai, Cheo, Bula-Sing and Nagar-Chao
were famous Kalash rulers in the 12th through 14th centuries AD. Their fellow
tribesmen in Afghanistan were known as Red Kafirs. The thriving Kalash culture
began to fall in 1320 AD., when Shah Nadir Raees subjugated and converted the
people to lslam. The villages of Drosh, Sweer, Kalkatak, Beori, Ashurate,
Shishi, Jinjirate and adjacent valleys in southern Chitral were the last Kalash
villages subjected to mass conversion in the 14th century. The Kalash were
living in just three Chitral valleys, Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir, by the time
Amir of Afghanistan forcefully converted to Islam the Red Kafirs on the other
side of the border in 1893 renaming the area Nuristan. Villages of the
converted Red Kafirs in Chitral are known as Sheikhanandeh – the villages of
converted ones. The Kalash, as well as the Sheikh community, are popular for
domestic and foreign tourism because of their unique culture. The Kalash area
is a hub of ecotourism activities. With the opening of the Lowari Tunnel on the
road to Peshawar and the proposed road to Tajikistan over the Dorah Pass, the
Kalash and Chitral will be linked with the cultural centres of Pakistan,
Afghanistan and Central Asia by all-weather land routes.

attractions.title: Ziarat Marble Hill
attractions.description:
Ziarat Marble District Mohmand
 It is one of the most premium and expensive marble types that are locally extracted in Pakistan.

attractions.title: Jale Gudar Park
attractions.description: Swat Road

attractions.title: Balahisar Fort
attractions.description: The gigantic structure of the Balahisar fort was built by the Sikh in 1834. During the British era, it was declared as the headquarters of Frontier Corps, after the partition it was converted into a military museum, and there was a ceremonial change of guards which took place every day 10 mins before sunset. The famous Koh-e-Noor diamond which the British Empire as part of their crown jewels, was taken by the Sikhs inside Balahisar fort from the Afghan rulers, and afterward when the East India Company annexed Peshawar in 1849, it was acquired by them and later presented to Her Majesty Queen Victoria.

attractions.title: Changla Galli
attractions.description: Changla Gali is one of the tourist mountain resorts of the Galiyat area. It has an elevation of 2559 m. During British rule, it was the headquarters of the Northern Command School of Musketry. Changla Galli is a picturesque hill station and tourist destination in Pakistan, situated in the Abbottabad District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. It is part of the larger Galyat range, which includes other popular hill stations like Murree, Nathiagali, and Ayubia.

attractions.title: Beshai Meadows
attractions.description:
Kalam, Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan Bishai meadow is
one of the most beautiful places in kalam valley. It took 3 to 3.5 hours hiking
from boyun village to reach this amazing place

attractions.title: Shogran
attractions.description:
Shogran, one of the most beautiful plateaus in the valley,
is situated 34 kilometers from Balakot via Kewai. To reach this quaint place,
take a side road on the right after passing through Kewai. From here it is a
steep 8 kilometers asphalt road to Shogran. Surrounded by thick pine forests at
an altitude of 7747 feet, the summer climate of Shogran is very mild and
pleasant. One of the nicer places to visit is Shogran's Forest Rest House. From
the grassy lawns of the rest house, one can see breathtaking panoramic views of
snow-covered mountains. Kaghan Valley's highest peaks, such as Musa Ka Musalla
(4419 m), Makra (3885 m), and Malika Parbat (5290 m), are visible from here. For
those wishing to stay for the night or have a meal, there are a number of medium
and high-standard hotels in Shogran. For more information on hotels please
consult the list of hotels.

attractions.title: Donga Gali
attractions.description:
Donga Gali is one of the towns of the Galiyat area
of Ayubia National Park , at an altitude of
2,500 meters (8,200 ft.) in northern Pakistan .
Donga Gali is located in Nathia Gali Union Council (subdivision) of Abbottabad District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province. It is 3
kilometers (1.9 mi) from Nathia Gali .
 During British Rule ,
Donga Gali served as a sanatorium to British soldiers and contained a hotel,
church and a post office. The area was also visited by Europeans, who also had
houses on the southern slopes of the nearby Mukshpuri
Mountains .

attractions.title: Miranjani (jannat pur)
attractions.description: Miranjani is the highest peak in Galiyat Region. Which is located at the elevation of 2,992 meters (9,816 ft.), in Abbottabad District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

attractions.title: Kalakot
attractions.description:
Kalakot
is a locality in Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and
has an elevation of 1,267 meters. KalaKot is situated nearby to the localities
Binarai and Rahat Kot. K alakot is a beautiful village located in an unmatched valley of Swat. It
is seen from far away and its scenery is praiseworthy. it is always in a full
spring because of trading and marketing.

attractions.title: Siri Paye
attractions.description:
A wonderful excursion from Shogran is a visit to Siri and
Paya. A rugged eight-kilometer road climbs 2300 feet through thick pine forest
to the top of Paya ridge, a lush green meadow with spectacular views of Makra,
Malika Parbat, and Musa ka Musala. One can also see varieties of wild alpine
flowers on the rolling grassy slopes of Paya. Visitors can then hike up Makra
(Spider) Mountain, which is 12743 feet from sea level. From Paya, trekkers must
climb around 2000 feet to reach the top of Makra, on the border between Kaghan
Valley and Azad Kashmir's Neelum Valley. This mountain climb is recommended
only for those who have previous experience in high-altitude hiking, are
familiar with the mountain wilderness safety rules, and are properly equipped.
Siri is a small meadow with a pond on the way to Paya. One can stop here for a
while for rest and refreshment. This place also has a small forest rest house
and some tea stalls. Travelers enjoy sipping hot tea from one of the stalls
while soaking in the majestic views of snow-covered mountains reflected in the
lake.

attractions.title: Skyland
attractions.description: Skyland is a beautiful place located in Upper Dir and at the top of Karo Dara and Nihag Dara, some parts of the sky land attached to district swat which distance about 33 Km from Khagram Bazar and 37 km from Wari. The spot is located at an altitude of about 10,300 feet from sea level.

attractions.title: Seri Bahlol
attractions.description: Seri Bahlol, also Sahr-i Bahlol or Sahri Bahlol, is a small village situated close to Takht Bhai in Mardan. It is a beautiful site with a number of archeological thrones which attracts tourists. This site is located near Takht Bhai and is at a distance of 70 km from Peshawar. This historical site contains the ruins of Buddhists which were built during the reign of Kushan Khan and are still present in a strong position. Ancient things like statues, coins, utensils and jewelry are usually found here. Since 1980 it has also been included in the list of world cultural heritage of UNESCO.

attractions.title: GFC Zipline
attractions.description: Running track Horse Riding Cricket Football Zip line Paintball Archer About 850m running track Badminton Tennis Wall climbing Squash Separate Gym for male and female Riders lounge Coffee Zone(Taste of all items are really good and reasonable price) Playground for kids You would love the sound of birds. This place is well maintained by Army.

attractions.title: Sherkot toi
attractions.description: Sherkot Toi is a picturesque village located in the Kohat district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Nestled amidst rolling hills and verdant fields, it offers a tranquil retreat from urban life. The village is known for its traditional charm, friendly community, and local culture, making it a hidden gem for those seeking an authentic rural experience. With its stunning landscapes and warm hospitality, Sherkot Toi provides a glimpse into the rich heritage and natural beauty of the region.

attractions.title: Saidgai Lake
attractions.description:
Saidgai Lake is situated in the Hindukush chain of mountains, interspersed
by several small and large lakes, which runs from the western edges of the
Pamir plateau, west of the Karakoram. The mountains have snow- covered tops and
are crossed by' some minor glaciers. Saidgai Lake is located in the peripheries
of Swat and Dir Mountain ranges and serves as a huge reservoir of water for
Hushirai Khwar (Stream), Dir. The lake can be accessed through three different
trails and sides: Hushirai valley, Dir, Sultan, upper Swat and Sakhra Lalko,
upper Swat. The Lalko (name of village) trail to the lake is the easiest and
breathtaking. A jeepable and unmetalled road ends in the beautiful and exotic
valley of Lalko where you’re trekking and hiking chapter starts. From here,
continuous trekking for almost seven to eight hours will lead you to your
desired destination. On the way, dark green pine, conifer and cedar forests
keep you cool and refreshed; and small scurrying streams quench your
unappeasable thirst (Tip: Own bottled water advisable). On the way, you will
come across a vast pasture, which is called Gabin Jabba (Honey marshes) in the local vernacular. The pastures wear a blanket of countless arid
innumerable variety of flowers of different shades that tempt different species
of rare birds and insects. The best season to visit and explore the lake is
during the months of July to September. In the remaining, a thick coat of snow
covers the lakes and makes difficult for the observer to differentiate it from
the surrounding landscapes. Saidgai is considered as one of the largest lakes
in the area and several adventure loving people swarm the area to discover and explore
this spectacular jewel of nature.

attractions.title: Mandur Top
attractions.description: Mandur is a mountain in Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and has an elevation of 1,460 meters. Mandur is situated nearby to the area Shamizai and the locality Baidara. Swat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan The middle of swat. 80% swat can be seen from this top.

attractions.title: Samundar Katha Lake
attractions.description: Samundar Katha Lake is located in Barra Gali (Nathiagali), is 35 KM from Abbottabad and 95 KM away from Islamabad, and offers zipline, boating, horse, riding, camping, and other watersports activities. The lake is surrounded by rolling hills and lush greenery, providing a serene and scenic environment. The pristine blue waters of the lake contrast beautifully with the green landscape. Samundar Katha Lake offers a range of recreational activities for visitors. Boating and fishing are popular pastimes here. Tourists can rent paddleboats and rowboats to explore the lake or simply relax while enjoying the tranquil surroundings. Fishing is allowed, and the lake is home to a variety of fish species.

attractions.title: Madaglasht Valley
attractions.description:
Khowar (Chitrali) and Persian Tourist attractions. Mixed
Chitrali and Persian culture, various handicrafts, Gocharsar Waterfall, treks
to the Goleen and Laspur valleys of Chitral, and to the Dir Kohistan valleys.
Sighting of various animals and birds. Daily transport (4x4) is available
between Drosh and Madaglasht at specified times. Travel time is three hours
from Drosh to the main village of the valley. It is recommended that a 4x4
vehicle be hired in Chitral and Drosh to access the valley. Local family guest
houses are available. For large tourist groups, it is advisable to carry tents
and sleeping bags. There are few opportunities to purchase food in the valley
but traditional cuisine may also be available. It is advisable to carry bottled
or boiled water for drinking.

attractions.title: Dadahara Park
attractions.description:
Dadahara Park in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is one of the world’s most
beautiful, peaceful, and serene places. The park’s name translates to The
Beauty of Flowers, which lives up to its name. With gorgeous trees and tranquil
surroundings, you’ll have plenty of time to enjoy yourself during your trip.
 The
Dadahara Park Swat is a natural wonder and is the highest point in Swat Valley.
From here, you can see breathtaking views of the valley unmatched by any other
place in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Dadahara Park Mingo is just below the mountain’s
peak and around a kilometer from Jarral Shaheed Park. The area has a variety of
scenic spots for photography and trekking. The best time to visit the park is
spring when the weather conditions are perfect for outdoor activities.

attractions.title: Marghazar White Palace
attractions.description: There are several things that keep pushing me, over and over, to visit the Marghazar Valley in Swat: Mount Elum, the lush green gorgeous landscape, serene environment, its historical sacredness, and above all, the White Palace of the state era in its lap.
