attractions.title: Blind Lake
attractions.description: Blind lake or Jarba Zhou lake is a scenic lake IN  Shigar. Although this lake is in District Shigar. the blind lake is nearly 30 minutes’ drive from Skardu city. The lake is on the way to the Shigar district from Skardu. A pearl and a hidden gem for adventure lovers. Visitors can enjoy walks on sand and rocks and lush green grass. A hidden pearl between mountains and a famous Cold desert Sarfaranga Skardu. Most importantly this lake is on the legendary route of K-2, the world’s second highest mountain.

attractions.title: Sarfaranga Cold Desert
attractions.description:
Sarfaranga Cold Desert is located in the Shigar District at a height of 7,500 feet on the way to Shigar Valley. Nature unfolds itself with a vast variety in this desert. The desert is surrounded by mountains and the Indus river is flowing nearby. The calmness of a desert is at its best a surprising and mesmerizing experience with sunset at top of sand dunes.
Annual Sarfaranga Cold Desert Jeep Rally is organized in the highest cold desert in the world, with the aim to promote adventure tourism in Gilgit-Baltistan and boost the local economy of the remote region. 
Besides the rally, the festival also features activities like free-style polo, boating, river rafting, sword dances, musical performances, and rock climbing.
More than 100 jeep racers and bikers participate in the rally, including women drivers each year.

attractions.title: Keris Valley
attractions.description: Keris valley is located in District Ghanche, which is 70 km from Khaplu City and 33 km from Skardu City. It is known as the gateway to Ghanche. The famous pedestrian bridge named 'Door to Heaven' is located in this valley. The valley also hosts one of the oldest hydropower stations, the hundreds years’ oldest canal, the Astana of Hazrat Mir Mukhtar and Ali Mosavi, the confluence of the Indus and Shyok Rivers, and the House of Peer of Noorbakhshia. It is the last village of Ghanche before entering Skardu District, so the residents Keris often travel to Skardu for work and shopping instead of Khaplu. Keris is famous for its lush green fields and ancient/historic houses. Tourists receive a warm welcome from hospitable locals. The best time to visit is during the Cherry Blossom season or summer.

attractions.title: Barah Valley
attractions.description: Barah Valley, located on the bank of the Shyok River and a 20-minute drive from Khaplu, is 100 km east of Skardu. Known for its beauty and numerous fish farms, it is one of Khaplu's unexplored gems. The valley features a famous lake at its top and many natural springs. The locals are simple, industrious, and hospitable, living an organic lifestyle with unique culture and festivals. Barah Valley is a fantastic place to visit and enjoy its serene, breathtaking landscape.

attractions.title: Haldi Cones
attractions.description: Haldi Cones are granite mountains in Haldi village, Ghanche. They can be seen from Khaplu town, Yuchung Masherbrum viewpoint, and Machulu village. To see them up close, visit Haldi village which is 25 km from Khaplu.

attractions.title: Chorbat Valley
attractions.description: Chorbat Valley is a part of the Shyok river valley split between Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan and Indian-administered Ladakh. In Pakistan, it's located in Khaplu tehsil of Ghanche District, and in India, it's in Nubra tehsil of Leh district. Chorbat Valley runs from the edge of Khaplu to Chalunka village in Nubra. In the 18th century, the Khan of Chorbat moved his capital from Siksa (originally named "Chorbat") to Turtuk. These two villages, now in Pakistan and India, are the largest in the Chorbat region.

attractions.title: Kharfaq Lake
attractions.description: Kharfaq Lake is located 2 km (away from the Kharfaq village and is around a 3-hour hike. The lake is a high-altitude natural lake in the Karakoram mountain range in Kharfaq Valley, District Ghanche. Renowned for its indigenous fish species, including thousands of trout and desi fish, the lake and its surroundings are a vital wildlife habitat. The best time to visit is July and August, while in winter, the snow-covered lake offers stunning views.

attractions.title: Ghanche Lake
attractions.description: Ghanche Lake, locally known as "Khenpi Tso," is situated at 4,600 meters above sea level in Ghanche Nullah. It is surrounded by lush pastures, diverse mountain flowers, glaciers, crystal-clear streams, and hills, creating a breathtaking atmosphere for tourists. The lake's unique feature is its awe-inspiring view of several of the world's highest peaks, including K2 (8,611m), Broad Peak (8,047m), Gashabrum-4 (7,925m), Gashabrum-3 (7,952m), Gashabrum-2 (8,035m), K6 (7,281m), and K7 (6,934m), as well as Hrnami Ka Peak (6,325m) and Chogho Lingsa Peak (6,325m).

attractions.title: Chaqchan Mosque
attractions.description: The Chaqchan Mosque meaning “The Miraculous Mosque” is located in the city of Khaplu at an elevated point and can be viewed from the Khaplu Valley unobstructed. Dating from 1370, the mosque is one of the oldest mosques in the region, and dates from the time when the area's populace converted from Buddhism to Islam. It is a perfect blend of Tibetan, Mughal and Persian style of architecture. It is a double story structure with two winter prayer rooms on the lower level and the main prayer hall on the top floor. This upper floor is wrapped around with a beautiful verandah on all four sides. The mosque consists of a traditional cribbage-and-cator technique, involving stone, adobe, timber and mud. The Chaqchan Jamia Mosque is an exemplary specimen of traditional architecture and it is considered to be one of the most beautiful mosque buildings in Gilgit-Baltistan. According to local accounts, Syed Amir Kabir Ali Hamdani constructed the mosque on an old Buddhist site while preaching Islam in the region.

attractions.title: Gondogoro Pass
attractions.description:
Gondogoro Pass, standing at an elevation of 5,585 meters, is situated in the Ghanche District of the Baltistan region in Pakistan, about 25 km south of K2, the world's second-highest peak. This mountain pass connects the Gondogoro Glacier to the southwest with the Vigne Glacier to the northeast.
On the southwest side, the route descends into Hushe village, home to the highest settlements in Ghanche District. Most climbers and trekkers approach Gondogoro Pass from the northeast side. In 1986, a route was established that connects Concordia in the upper Baltoro Glacier to the Hushe Valley by crossing the Gondogoro Pass. Since then, the pass has become a popular destination for trekkers and climbers, offering stunning views of the Karakoram's 8,000-meter peaks.
While popular, the Gondogoro La presents challenging conditions. It involves Class 4 climbing that necessitates the use of crampons. On the northeast side, steep snow slopes with angles of up to 50 degrees pose avalanche risks and often require fixed ropes. The southwest side features a longer, continuous 50-degree slope, with potential rockfall and avalanche hazards, which may require up to 300 meters of fixed ropes.

attractions.title: Khaplu Valley
attractions.description:
Khaplu, the administrative and commercial center of Ghanche District in Gilgit-Baltistan, is a beautiful and scenic destination. Renowned for its cultural richness, natural beauty, and diverse traditions, it offers numerous picnic spots and tourist points. Khaplu serves as the gateway to Hushe Valley, leading to remarkable lakes, hiking trails, peaks, and glaciers. With vibrant fruit orchards, breathtaking views, high mountains, and architectural heritage, Khaplu is an unrivaled tourist attraction, embodying the beauty of Pakistan.
Khaplu Valley offers many hotels and guest houses, including the famous PTDC Khaplu Motel, PWD Guest House, and Serena Khaplu Fort. Serena Khaplu Fort, once a royal residence now restored by the Agha Khan Foundation, serves local Balti dishes and functions as a heritage hotel.

attractions.title: Saling Valley
attractions.description:
Saling Valley is a scenic tourist destination in the Ghanche district of Pakistan with its breathtaking landscapes and cultural heritage. it offers visitors a unique experience of natural beauty and traditional life. Saling Valley is a beautiful village renowned for its breathtaking views, outstanding scenery, and high-altitude landscapes, making it a popular tourist hotspot.
Saling is a doorway to Hushe Valley as well as a very nice camping spot just beside a lake. There is a wonderful fish farm in Saling that offers delicious fish feasts. Many springs are also present in this area including a hot spring which is good for bathing in the winters as well. 
The Saling valley was the king’s empire. The royal Amacha family’s Fort was also there in the Saling valley. But this fort is not as big as in the Khaplu mal. That’s the reason that this fort is not as famous as the one in Khaplu mal.
The land of the Saling valley is fertile to grow wheat, potatoes, tomatoes, and other vegetables. The people of this valley are famous for their hospitality. The crime rate in this valley is 0%. No case has been registered in the police stations here in the last several years.

attractions.title: Hushe Valley
attractions.description:
Hushe is the last village of the Ghangche District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. The valley is renowned for its granite rocks, snow-capped peaks, and stunning beauty. The valley is known for the surrounding high mountains of the Karakoram range, including several peaks above six thousands meters like Laila Peak, K6, and K7. Murtaza peak is 5,100 m just behind K6 base camp and is considered the epicenter of trekkers and beginners. There are many sub-valleys in the area, including Gondogor Charkusa, Nagma, Nanbroq and Mashabrum.

Hushe village was one of the extremely remote and impoverished valleys of Baltistan. With the opening of Adventure Tourism by 1960s, Hushe Valley has become the epicenter of trekking and mountaineering activities. Hushe is no longer the poorest of villages, as its popularity as a trekking and climbing destination continues to grow. Climbers and trekkers come all the way from Baltoro Glacier, Concordia and K-2 via Gondogoro Pass, descend into Hushe village to reach Skardu District. Access to the Gasherbrum peaks is also possible going north up through Hushe Valley.

attractions.title: Thalley Valley
attractions.description:
Thalley is a lush green valley in Ghanche, located 35 km northwest of the district headquarters Ghanche and 110 km from Skardu city. Situated at 2,647m above sea level, it falls in the single cropping zone. The main occupation of the inhabitants of the valley is agriculture. 

Thalley Broq is an attractive place for camping and hiking. The milky nights of Thalley Valley during the full moons presents unforgettable moments to the tourists. It also provides track to K2 base camp. Thalley Valley also offers a nice track to Shigar Valley via Thalley La and gives an opportunity to view a series of snowcapped mountains.

attractions.title: Burst Valley
attractions.description: Burst Valley is located in Ghizer District of Gilgit-Baltistan. It is six hours from Gilgit city at an elevation of about 10,720 feet lies 22 km from Shandur Top. Barsat Valley in Ghizer District, Gilgit-Baltistan, is a prime destination for tourists. The valley's stunning natural beauty, including its scenic landscapes and abundant trout streams, makes it a popular spot for nature lovers and anglers. Its proximity to Shandur Top, known for the annual polo festival, adds to its appeal. Visitors can immerse themselves in the local culture, with the Khowar language adding to the unique experience.

attractions.title: Shandur Pass
attractions.description: A twisting road of 61 km from Gupis valley passing through lush green fields and forests with a view of the flowing river and icy peaks will lead the tourists to this charming valley. From springs of crystal clear waters to lakes and rivers of deep blue water, there are all colors of natural beauty in Phandar Valley. The very first glance of this valley will eliminate all fatigue of journey and will energize the visitors with its mesmerizing views.

attractions.title: Khalti Lake
attractions.description: Khalti Lake is situated in Khalti village at an altitude of about 2217 m (7274ft) from sea level. The lake is known for its habitat of trout fish. The lake usually freezes in winter season and people can easily walk on it. It hosts Khalti Ice Hockey Festival in January every year which is an annual calendar event of GB Tourism department.

attractions.title: Phandar Valley
attractions.description:
Phander Valley is located in District Ghizer of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan at 1,454ft above sea level. Phander Valley is famous for its most beautiful and attractive valleys, lush green fields, deep blue lakes, and the river flowing across it; which is commonly called “Little Kashmir”. Phandar Valley is easily accessible from both from Gilgit and Chitral sides. It takes 5 to 6 hours from the main city Gilgit to reach Phander Valley. Phander Lake is one of the most famous tourist spots in the entire region. The name of Ghizer also comes from the name of a village ‘Ghizer’ which is situated in the locality of Phander. The deep blue Phandar Lake is beautifully landscaped and is primarily a habitat for trout fish. The people of Phander Valley are simple, peaceful, and hospitable. The people of the valley speak Khowar language.
A large number of tourists visit Phandar Valley every year to enjoy the beautiful view of nature. PTDC, Phandar Rest Rest House, and various other hotels are existed here to provide accommodation facilities to visiting tourists.

attractions.title: Yasin Valley
attractions.description: The Yasin Valley with spectacular scenic beauty, is a high mountain valley in Hindu Kush Mountains in Ghizer district. In summer season, the valley becomes a touristic hub for national and international tourists and adventure lovers because of its scenic beauty and treks from Darkut to Chitral via Broghal pass and Baba Ghundi via Chilingi pass. There is an annual festival, Tukhm Rezi, celebrated in spring season or in the beginning of summer. It is a centuries old agricultural festival of Yasin Valley during which people play traditional polo matches, enjoy horse jump, dancing on traditional tunes and preparation of traditional cuisines such as Diram, Diram Phiti etc.

attractions.title: Karumber Lake
attractions.description: One of the most beautiful, pristine and pure lakes of Pakistan at an elevation of 4272m. KarUmber Lake lies on the boundary of Broghil valley in Chitral and Ishkoman valley in Gilgit-Baltistan. It is the 33rd highest lake in the world and one of the most biologically active lakes on earth.

attractions.title: Ishkoman
attractions.description: The Ishkoman valley lies in the north of Ghizer District bordering Afghanistan and the Pamir Wakhan Corridor. It is located at a range of altitudes, from 2,100 to 3,700 m. Running north to south to join the Gilgit valley, the Ishkoman Valley divides the Karakoram Range from the Hindu Kush. Incorporated into Pakistan in 1972, it is about 100 kilometres to Chatorkhand and Phakora to the road head at Imit. There are five possible treks from the Ishkoman River through Phakora across the 4,600-metre Naltar Pass, 55 kilometres long, restricted-zone trek to the Chipursan valley, Koz Sar 6,677 metres, Chillinji Pass 5,291 metres and Karumber Pass 4,343 metres. The Ishkoman Pass is well used by locals going to Darkot or upper Chitral, but the route is narrower, higher, less scenic and less populated than the Asumbar Pass.

attractions.title: Gahkuch
attractions.description: Gahkuch is the capital of Ghizer at the distance of 72km from Gilgit City on Shandur Gilgit Road. It is surrounded by mountains on the bank of the Gilgit River. There are all types of accommodations including PTDC hotel for tourists. It is a lush green valley with high mountains. The view of the Gilgit River in Gahkuch is very of beauty due to the wideness of the river in this area.

attractions.title: Chatorkhand
attractions.description: Chatorkhand is the main town in Ishkoman Valley along the Karambar River. It is a deep valley with high mountains. Along the Karambar River, greenery provides a very wonderful view with brownish mountains and snow-capped peaks at the distance.

attractions.title: BORITH LAKE
attractions.description:
Borith Lake is a lake in the Hunza district of Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan. Borith is a hamlet in the surroundings of the Borith Lake to the northwest of Husseini, a village near Ghulkin, Gojal, in the upper Hunza. The altitude of Borith is roughly 2,600 m (8,500 feet) above sea level.
It was a popular hunting place for the Mir of Hunza during winters particularly for birds. A small house was built for the Mir on a hill surrounding the lake just on the edge. Today this house is known as the Borith Lake Hotel. Borith Lake has reduced in size and become brackish over the years due to a reduction in the underground seepage that feeds it - a result of receding glaciers and the impact of climate change. The lake is an important bird sanctuary for migrating wildfowl (ducks, geese and swans). The best time to see these migrating birds is between the months of March and June, when they make their way to the cooler climes of Central Asia and between September and November, as they return to the warmer parts of the Southern Pakistan.

attractions.title: Passu Glacier
attractions.description: Passu Glacier  is situated in the south side of Passu village, in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Passu Peak is situated behind the glacier. This glacier is linked with Batura Glacier and many other glaciers in Batura Muztagh mountain range.

attractions.title: Khunjerab Pass
attractions.description: Khunjerab Pass is located in Sost Village of Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan Pakistan. It often referred to as the "Gateway to China," is one of the world's highest international border crossings. At an elevation of 4,693 meters (15,397 feet), this breathtaking mountain pass connects Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan with China’s Xinjiang region. The name "Khunjerab" is derived from two words of the local Wakhi language: "Khun" means blood and "Jerab" means a creek coming from a spring or waterfall. It translates to "Valley of Blood" in the local Wakhi language, reflecting the pass's challenging terrain and history. The Khunjerab Pass is closed during winter months because of harsh weather.

attractions.title: Sost Valley
attractions.description:
Sost is a beautiful village as well as an attractive tourist destination in Gojal  Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan situated at an elevation of 2,800 meters above sea level. It is located at a distance of 184 km from the main Gilgit city on Karakoram Highway before the China Border at Khunjerab Pass (the highest border crossing in the world).
Sost is the last Pakistani town on the Karakoram Highway before the
Pakistan and China have opened border for trade and tourism. All traffic, crossing the Pakistan-China border, passes through the Sost village where the first formal Dry Port facilitates customs clearance and other formalities for goods moving from China to the commercial centers of Pakistan. Accordingly, the Pakistani immigration and customs departments are established here.
The people speak the Wakhi and Brushki Languages in Sost Village. The Sost village is a perfect tourist destination where the visiting tourists admire the peaceful environment and high level of hospitality of the local people.
To reach Sost Village one can either fly to Islamabad and drive to Hunza and later into Sost which is the last village inside Pakistan on the Karakoram Highway before the Chinese border or one can also fly into Kashgar or Urumqi in China and drive into crossing the Pak-China border at Khunjerab Pass, where the first village inside Pakistan is Sost. In winter due to heavy snow, the border crossing between China and Pakistan through Khunjerab Pass remains block.

attractions.title: Kilik Pass and Mintaka Pass
attractions.description: Kilik Pass and Mintaka Pass, located to the north of Misgar, have a deep historical significance as they were integral parts of the ancient Silk Road. The historic Mintika pass that connects Pakistan with China. The historic Kilik pass is also located in Misgar and it leads travelers to Afghanistan. These passes served as the customary caravan routes connecting Pakistan and India to Tashkurgan Tashkurgan before the Karakoram Highway was established.

attractions.title: Misgar Valley
attractions.description: Misgar Valley is located in the Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, near the borders with China and Afghanistan. Misgar Valley is one of the most beautiful and geographically important regions of Gilgit-Baltistan. Misgar is home to the Mintika pass that connects Pakistan with China. The historic Kilik pass is also located in Misgar and it leads travelers to Afghanistan. The historic “Kalam Darchi Fort” constructed by the Britishers to keep a watch on Russian and Chinese advances, is also located in Misgar.

attractions.title: Karimabad Valley
attractions.description: Karimabad formerly known as Baltit, is located in Hunza District of Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan. Karimabad is famous for its rich cultural heritage, stunning landscapes, and warm hospitality. It's also known for the ancient Baltit Fort and its association with the spiritual leader, Prince Karim Aga Khan.

attractions.title: Kalamdarchi Fort,
attractions.description: Kalamdarchi Fort, named after a naked saint was built during British regime in 1932-1933 to check ingresses from China and Afghanistan. It remained the abode of Gilgit Scouts, NLI and Pak Army TPS and underwent metamorphic changes during this period.

attractions.title: Baltit For
attractions.description:
Ancient Baltit fort is located in District Hunza of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Baltit Fort was the capital of Hunza State, and the old settlement is still intact to this day.
Baltit Fort is a prominent historical site in Pakistan and this place offers a panoramic view of Hunza Valley and the highest mountain peaks in Pakistan. Baltit Fort was the home of Ayashkutz royal family of Hunza for 700 years. Formerly known as Kanjut, Hunza was an independent principality ruled by a hereditary monarch named Mir Tham in the local Burushaski language. In the 19th century, Baltit Fort was part of the Great Game. In 1891, as part of an overall strategy to contain the Russians, British troops invaded Hunza and eventually occupied Baltit Fort and Hunza state. The structure of the fortress has undergone many changes over the years. The fort was abandoned in 1945, and Mir Ghazanfar Ali Khan later donated the fort to Baltit Heritage Trust. The Aga Khan Trust for Culture renovated the Baltit fort and is on the tentative list of UNESCO’s world heritage sites since 2004. The Baltit Fort now stands as a heritage site in Pakistan to be visited by tourists from all over the world.

attractions.title: Altit Fort
attractions.description:
Altit Fort, situated in the Hunza Valley of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, is a historic marvel dating back over 900 years. Perched on a rocky hilltop overlooking the Hunza River, it stands as a testament to the region's rich cultural heritage and strategic significance along the ancient Silk Road. Constructed in the 11th century by the Baltit people, ancestors of today's Hunza community, Altit Fort is one of the oldest surviving forts in the area. Over centuries, it has served as a stronghold for various rulers and clans, witnessing the region's historical transformations.
Today, Altit Fort is a meticulously preserved heritage site that offers visitors a glimpse into the architectural prowess and lifestyle of the ancient Baltit civilization. With breathtaking views of the valley and mountains, it remains a cherished destination for tourists and history enthusiasts alike, symbolizing the enduring legacy of the Hunza Valley's cultural and historical heritage.

attractions.title: Aliabad Hunza
attractions.description: Aliabad is the administrative and commercial center of the Hunza District. The town is located in a relatively wide section of the Hunza Valley, in the northeastern corner of the Karakoram range, between two forks of the Hunza River. Like most localities in Hunza, Aliabad lies along the Karakoram Highway, which crosses this mountainous district.

attractions.title: Rakaposhi
attractions.description:
Rakaposhi, meaning "Shining Wall" or Dumani, meaning "Mother of Mist" in Burushaski, is a prominent mountain in the Karakoram range, located in District Nagar of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan standing 7,788 meters (25,550 ft) tall. It is notable for its uninterrupted 6,000-meter descent from summit to base. Rakaposhi, the 27th-highest mountain in the world, offers stunning views of the Nagar Valley from the Karakoram Highway. Rakaposhi's first successful ascent was in 1958 by a British expedition. It is home to endangered species like the Marco Polo sheep, snow leopards, and brown bears.
Rakaposhi View Point, also known as the "Zero Point of Rakaposhi," offers the closest view of the stunning Rakaposhi mountain and its surrounding natural beauty. Located on the Karakoram Highway (KKH) in Ghulmet village, Nagar Valley, it is a popular stop for travelers between Gilgit and Hunza. The Karakoram Highway, more than just a road connecting Pakistan and China, is lined with scenic spots, cultural heritage, and archaeological sites, attracting tourists to pause and explore.
At Rakaposhi View Point, visitors can relax, enjoy breathtaking views of the 7,788-meter Rakaposhi, and sit by the glacier-fed streams. In summer, many dip their feet in the cool water while taking in the scenery. Over the years, the viewpoint has developed with improved infrastructure, driven by increasing tourist numbers. The mountain, glacier, greenery, and flowing streams make it a must-visit spot for nature lovers.

attractions.title: Sikandarabad Valley
attractions.description: Sikandarabad, a picturesque village in the Nagar District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, serves as the administrative center of the district. Nestled along the Karakoram Highway (KKH), Sikandarabad is situated in a mountainous region within the Karakoram Range, near the base camp of the renowned Rakaposhi mountain. Directly across from Sikandarabad lies the majestic Himalaya Range.

attractions.title: Kacheli Lake
attractions.description: The ethereal Kacheli Lake lies in the Miacher Valley of the Nagar District. It is situated amidst the captivating Kacheli Meadows, this high-altitude lake enchants visitors with its untouched beauty.

attractions.title: Rush Lake
attractions.description: Rush Lake is one of Pakistan’s highest lakes at a staggering altitude of 4694 meters above sea level. The pristine waters and breathtaking surroundings offer an awe-inspiring experience that will stay with you forever.

attractions.title: Hispar Glacier
attractions.description:
Prepare to be amazed by the majestic Hispar Glacier, stretching a colossal 49 kilometers. Trekking from Biafo Glacier to Hisper Glacier leads you to the mesmerizing Snow Lake, a frozen glacial paradise.

This expedition is a dream come true for adventure enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.

attractions.title: Natural Cricket Stadium
attractions.description:
The world’s highest natural Cricket Stadium is located in Pissan Valley at District Nagar of Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan at an elevation of 8,500 feet above sea level. It came under the spotlight in January 2021 after sharing an astonishing picture of this stadium on social media by a local journalist. Natural Cricket Stadium Nagar became an aspiration for cricket lovers across Pakistan.

Natural Cricket Stadium is within walking distance of 1 hour from Pissan main Bazar. It is around 1.5 km above the Main Bazar. The Natural Stadium is located under the shoulder of the ferocious snow-covered Rakaposhi and Diran peaks. These treasures make this stadium more unique and stand out from the others. The Pisan Stadium catches huge fans within a moment of days. The reason is its natural aesthetical gifts. It has a lush green carpet under the mountain nest. This stadium is among the areas of tourism-boosting projects in GB. Cricket in highly favorable weather (20°C) in peak summer when the rest of the country faces scorching heat. This can only be possible in Natural Stadium Nagar. The weather of this area remains pleasant during summer and a bit troublesome during winter. The temperature never spikes above 25°C in summer. 

The world’s highest natural cricket stadium Pisan Nagar officially inaugurated by GB Government on Saturday. in this connection, a cricket Tournament was arranged by Sports Department GB; the Diamer and Nagar teams played the first game at the stadium, where provincial minister Fatehullah Khan was present as the  Chief Guest.

Chief Secretary Gilgit-Baltistan Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani on the occasion said that the government of Gilgit-Baltistan is planning to promote the culture of the stadium in order to groom the local cricketing talent of GB. We hope that players from this region will represent Pakistan in international tournaments. Moreover, we want to unlock the region’s touristic potential that will spur economic activity in nearby villages and bring livelihood to people at their doorstep,” he added.

attractions.title: Manthokha Waterfall
attractions.description:
Manthokha Waterfall is a stunning natural attraction located in the Kharmang Valley, approximately 80 kilometers from Skardu in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan. The waterfall drops from a height of about 180 feet, creating a mesmerizing view with lush greenery surrounding it. The crystal-clear water and the serene environment make it a perfect spot for nature lovers and photographers. The area is ideal for picnics, with several spots where visitors can relax and enjoy the natural beauty. There are opportunities for fishing and trout farming in the nearby streams.
Manthokha Waterfall is a must-visit destination for anyone exploring the Gilgit-Baltistan region, offering a tranquil escape into nature's beauty. The best time to visit Manthokha Waterfall is from May to September when the weather is pleasant, and the roads are accessible. During winter, the area can be quite cold, and access may be restricted due to snow. The waterfall is about a two-hour drive from Skardu. Hiring a local guide or driver is recommended as the roads can be challenging. Ensure your vehicle is suitable for rough terrains.
There are a few guesthouses and hotels in Kharmang Valley, but booking in advance is advisable, especially during peak tourist season. Alternatively, you can stay in Skardu and plan a day trip to the waterfall.

attractions.title: Khamush Waterfall
attractions.description: The Khamush Waterfall in Kharmang Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, is a breathtaking natural wonder surrounded by scenic mountains and lush greenery. It's an ideal destination for nature lovers and adventurers, with its cascading water creating a mesmerizing display. Visiting this waterfall is a must for anyone exploring Gilgit-Baltistan.

attractions.title: Ghandus Lake
attractions.description: Ghandus is a small town in Kharmang Valley, about 130 kilometers from Skardu, known for its scenic beauty. Ghandus Lake, a hidden gem at 2,800 meters above sea level, offers breathtaking views with its turquoise waters and picturesque mountain backdrop. The 3-hour trek from Ghandus Valley is ideal in summer, with warm weather and clear skies perfect for hiking, trekking, and camping. The lush landscapes, blooming flowers, and orchards add to the valley's charm. Visitors can also experience the unique culture of the Balti people who live there.

attractions.title: Tolti Valley
attractions.description:
Tolti serves as the administrative capital of Kharmang District of Gilgit-Baltistan. It is located on the left bank of the Indus River, about 35 km southeast of the Indus-Shyok confluence. Historically, it was a trade route between Skardu and Kargil, however, the First Kashmir War's partition of the region ended this route.
Tolti Valley, nestled in the heart of the Kharmang District of Gilgit-Baltistan, offers breathtaking landscapes and rich cultural heritage. Known for its lush greenery, towering mountains, and serene rivers, the valley is a haven for nature enthusiasts and adventure seekers. Visitors can explore historical sites, and traditional villages that reflect the area's unique cultural blend. The valley's natural beauty and tranquil environment make it an ideal destination for those looking to experience the unspoiled charm of Gilgit-Baltistan.

attractions.title: Olding Valley
attractions.description:
Olding Valley, the last village of District Kharmang in Gilgit-Baltistan, is renowned for its stunning scenery, including mountains, lush fields, and the crystal-clear Indus River. The village is situated at 8,676 feet (2,644 m) above sea level, near the India-Pakistan border (LOC), it lies on the traditional trade route between Baltistan and Ladakh via Kargil. The village's small population relies on agriculture and livestock farming and has a rich cultural and historical heritage, highlighted by the tomb of Shaikh Ali Brolmo.

Inhabited predominantly by Tibetic peoples such as Baltis and Purigpas, the main languages are Balti and Purgi, however, while English and Urdu are widely spoken . Islam is the dominant faith. The village is known for various fruits, including apricot, apple, grapes, mulberry, cherry, and peach, which locals sell to earn income.

attractions.title: Mehdiabad Valley
attractions.description:
Mehdiabad Valley, formerly known as Parkuta, is one of the most beautiful valleys in District Kharmang, Gilgit-Baltistan. The old name Parkuta was changed to Mehdiabad by Sheikh Hassan Mehdi on the occasion of the birth of Imam Mehdi (as) in 1982 to commemorate the birth of Imam Mehdi (as). 

Mehdiabad Valley is located 62 km east of Skardu city. The valley encompasses five famous areas: Serling, Doqbar, Mehdiabad Khas, Bedong, and Pandah Village.

attractions.title: Pari Valley
attractions.description: Pari Valley, the heart of District Kharmang in Gilgit Baltistan, is a hidden gem known for its stunning suspension bridge and delicious Saspolo apples. The bridge, spanning a rushing river and offering breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and forests, attracts visitors seeking both thrill and beauty. Pari village is also renowned for its unique Saspolo apples, known for their crisp texture, juicy flavor, and distinctive red and green coloring. This charming destination combines natural splendor with delightful produce, making it a must-visit for an unforgettable experience.

attractions.title: Saspolo Apple
attractions.description:
The Kharmang Pari valley is renowned for its orchards, especially the unique Saspolo Apple, named after Saspolo village in Kargil, India. The valley's distinct climate and soil conditions create an ideal environment for these apples to thrive. Locals in the valley grow Saspolo Apples using traditional methods without artificial fertilizers or pesticides. They ensure the highest quality, resulting in delicious, healthy apples free from harmful chemicals. Each fall, Saspolo Apples are hand-harvested, carefully picked at perfect ripeness. They are then sorted, packaged, and shipped to markets and restaurants across Pakistan. Tourist visiting the area during apple season can enjoy the unique experience of biting into a freshly picked, sun-warmed apple bursting with flavor.

Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region produces 14 types of apples, yielding about 24,000 tons annually. However, the Saspolo variety is unique to Kharmang's Pari valley, where 90% of the 6,000 residents are involved in apple farming. To promote this indigenous variety of apple and support local growers, the Agriculture Department of Gilgit-Baltistan organizes an annual Saspolo Festival. The festival attracts hundreds with the apples' exquisite color, taste, and aroma.
